package_info.package_versions: all versions between January 31, 2021 and April 1, 2021 (compromised period)
package_info.why_malicious: The Codecov Bash Uploader script was maliciously modified to exfiltrate all environment variables, including sensitive credentials and secrets, from CI/CD environments to an attacker-controlled server. This enabled large-scale credential theft from any system using the compromised script.

execution_context.trigger: at runtime during CI/CD pipeline execution
execution_context.file_location: bash uploader script (e.g., codecov.sh) - compromised version

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime during CI/CD pipeline execution, the code reads all environment variables from the running process and sends them via HTTP POST to an attacker-controlled IP address, resulting in exfiltration of sensitive credentials and secrets.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code collects all environment variables, which often contain sensitive information such as API keys, tokens, and credentials, and transmits them to an external, untrusted server. This is a clear data exfiltration technique not present in legitimate uploader scripts.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Codecov Bash Uploader scripts are only expected to upload code coverage data to official Codecov servers. They should never transmit environment variables or sensitive data to unknown or hardcoded IP addresses.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate scripts may use curl to upload coverage reports to trusted endpoints, but never to send environment variables or secrets to untrusted or hardcoded external servers.
key_indicators: Exfiltration of all environment variables via network request
Use of curl to send data to a hardcoded, non-Codecov IP address
Presence of new or modified code in trusted scripts performing data theft
Outbound HTTP POST requests containing environment variable data

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains unauthorized access to Codecov's Bash Uploader script repository and modifies the script to include malicious data exfiltration logic.
attack_chain.leads_to: Distribution of the compromised Bash Uploader script to users

attack_chain.action: Developers and CI/CD systems unknowingly download and execute the tampered Bash Uploader script as part of their build and test pipelines.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code in trusted CI/CD environments

attack_chain.action: The malicious code reads all environment variables and sends them to the attacker's server via an outbound HTTP POST request.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives sensitive credentials, tokens, and secrets from victim environments

behavioral_signatures: Uploader scripts making outbound network requests to non-Codecov or hardcoded IP addresses
Unexpected exfiltration of environment variables during CI/CD pipeline execution
Presence of curl or wget commands sending environment data to untrusted endpoints
Modification of official Codecov Bash Uploader script to include data theft logic
file_indicators: Codecov Bash Uploader script (e.g., codecov.sh) with added or modified lines containing curl or wget commands targeting non-official endpoints
Presence of code that reads all environment variables (e.g., use of 'env' or similar) and transmits them externally
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS POST requests to unknown or suspicious IP addresses or domains during CI/CD jobs
Connections to IP addresses not associated with official Codecov infrastructure, especially during build/test pipeline execution
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor CI/CD pipeline scripts for unauthorized modifications, especially any that transmit environment variables externally. Flag any uploader or utility scripts that send data to non-official endpoints or hardcoded IP addresses. Use network monitoring to detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to suspicious IPs or domains during build/test jobs. Compare script hashes against known-good versions to detect tampering. Alert on the presence of curl or wget commands that transmit environment data outside the organization.
